ambient_trade.text: Bolts are fetching {gold} apiece in {town} this week. Good time to sell, good time to buy.
Anyone hauling salt out of {town}? I will pay {gold} a sack, fair price, no haggling tantrums.
Tip for the caravan folk: stock that sits in {town} for a week loses more than it gains. Move your goods.
Paying {gold} for good dyed cloth in {town}, coin on delivery. The ledger never lies.

encounter_trade_offer.text: {player}, a fair offer: {gold} for the lot, delivered to {town} without a single toll. I am not robbing you, I promise.
I can pay {gold} for your goods, {player}, which is a good price in {town} this season. Take it or leave it, but do not come back asking for more.
{player}, I would rather buy than fight. {gold} is on the table for safe passage to {town}. Bandits never pay, so you would be the first.

encounter_greeting.text: Ah, {player}, good to see you on this road! {persona} of {my_faction}, at your service. Care to trade some news, and maybe some wool?
Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Our caravans are headed for the same market, so let us keep this road peaceful and profitable.
{player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here. I have forgiven worse than your banners, but I keep a ledger, and you are now in it. Shall we talk terms before this turns ugly?

player_raided_my_village.text: Burning {village} was a poor trade, {player}. Ruined stock does not sell, and that is the only lesson that matters to me.
{player}, a private word. You burned {village} and I lost three bolts of wool. Name a price for the damage and we can still do business.
Who burned {village}? Half the wool route passes through there, and now my caravans take the long road and pay double the tolls.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}. Every war closes a road, and every closed road costs me coin. Wonderful.
Heralds in {my_faction} are shouting about {enemy_faction} again. Wars are bad for trade. Insurance rates will climb by the week.
War with {enemy_faction}, and {my_faction} will pay for it in tolls and lost cargo. I am writing this into the ledger.

peace_made.text: {my_faction} and {faction} have made peace. Good news for the wool route. Prices will settle and the tolls might finally stop climbing.
Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last, a treaty worth the parchment. Caravans can move without escorts, which saves me a fortune.
Ink is drying on the treaty between {my_faction} and {faction}. Lower risk means lower insurance, and lower insurance makes a happy ledger.

released_by_player.text: {player}, you let me go instead of ransoming me. That is the sort of deal I respect. Your name is already in my ledger in gold.
{player} released me without a ransom. Rare sight in these parts. Ransoms are a bad investment anyway, so well done, I say.
{player}, you let me walk without a ransom. I will not forget the ambush, and I will not forgive it either. Fair is fair.

beat_by_player.text: {player}, your {troop_count} men beat mine in the field. I lost a fortune in mail and horses. Fine. Now let us talk about who pays for the damage.
{player}, {troop_count} troops ended my fight today. I tallied the losses and they cost more than the battle was worth. Let us talk terms.
{player} beat me in the field with {troop_count} troops and I do not begrudge it. Victories cost less than wars, and you won this one fairly.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {fief} is under siege by {enemy_faction}. I can pay you well for relief, and the garrison will remember your name. Name your fee.
{player}, {enemy_faction} is at the gates of {fief}. Help me hold it and I will double whatever the crown offers you. Is that a deal?
{player}, my wool is stuck inside {fief} while {enemy_faction} blocks the road. Ride with me and I will cover the supply costs for the whole campaign.

ambient_complaint.text: Another toll gate outside {town}, and another cart robbed on the same road. Bandits never pay a single coin of tax, and I never get a receipt.
{rival} wants double for an escort again. Protection that costs more than the cargo is just robbery with manners.
{faction} raised the tolls again while the road to {town} keeps crumbling. Someone is pocketing the difference, and it is not the road.
Three of my carts were stripped on the road to {town} this month, and not one bandit paid a toll. Rude, that.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain on the road out of {town} again. Mud costs me a wheel a week, and the wheelwright charges me for the privilege.
Anyone know whether the {village} mill is running? Flour is cheap there and I have a buyer waiting in {town}.
Lag ate three of my ledger entries again. Forty tolls logged, half of them gone. Infuriating, but the rest still balance.
Lovely evening over {village}. Dry roads and steady weather keep prices calm. Long may it last.
